title: Enterprise Legal and Commercial Readiness v1 — Rig Relay

agpl_license_posture.upstream_lineage: Forked from mistralai/mistral-vibe (Apache-2.0). Codebase substantially diverged.
agpl_license_posture.attribution_obligations: UPSTREAM.md and ATTRIBUTION.md document lineage. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists upstream components.
agpl_license_posture.cla_requirement: CONTRIBUTING.md requires CLA. Maintainer reserves relicense rights.
agpl_license_posture.enterprise_impact: AGPL is a hard blocker for many enterprise procurement processes due to copyleft network-use clause. Dual-licensing strategy essential.

required_actions: Define commercial license terms (permissive, subscription-based, or OEM)
Determine pricing model: per-seat, per-tenant, usage-based, or flat enterprise
Address AGPL concerns explicitly in commercial terms
Provide license compatibility assurance for enterprise dependencies

gaps: No complete third-party dependency license inventory
attribution_obligations.recommendation: Produce full dependency license inventory. Add license compliance check to CI.

privacy_notice.current: Privacy notice alpha exists (docs/legal/privacy-notice-alpha.md). Usage data license alpha also exists.
gaps: Alpha notice is not finalized — marked as alpha/disclaimer
No data retention schedule linked from privacy notice
No cookie policy (though no cookies are used)
privacy_notice.recommendation: Finalize privacy notice. Add GDPR/CCPA supplements. Link to data inventory. Publish on static site.

telemetry_notice.current: Usage data doctrine is comprehensive. Product telemetry is first-party, enabled by default, and opt-out. Remote telemetry contribution is separately gated by consent scopes. Local operational observability is mandatory for governed operation. Enterprise audit/evidence is mandatory in enterprise mode.
gaps: No plain-language telemetry notice for end users that separates product telemetry (default-on, opt-out) from remote telemetry contribution (settings-controlled)
No disclosure of what specific data is collected in each of the four categories: product telemetry, remote telemetry contribution, local operational observability, and enterprise audit/evidence
No visual indicator in cockpit when product telemetry is active vs when remote contribution is enabled
Legal docs must distinguish product telemetry, remote contribution, local operational observability, and enterprise audit/evidence as separate control surfaces
telemetry_notice.recommendation: Create plain-language telemetry disclosure. Add telemetry/evidence status indicator to cockpit. Include four-category model in privacy notice. Distinguish product telemetry default-on/opt-out from remote contribution settings in all legal docs.

gaps: No defined roles (controller vs processor) for Rig Relay maintainer
dpa_readiness.recommendation: Draft DPA template. Define data processing roles. For local-first: user is controller, Rig Relay is not a processor. For hosted: Rig Relay becomes processor. Document clearly.

gaps: No warranty disclaimer (though AGPL includes implied)
terms_of_service.recommendation: Draft terms of service. For open-source: AGPL terms apply. For commercial: separate commercial terms.

gaps: No prohibition on using tool for attacks, malware, or illegal purposes
acceptable_use_policy.recommendation: Draft acceptable use policy. Include in terms of service and repository.

security_policy.recommendation: Consider bug bounty program for post-beta. Document security audit plans.

vulnerability_disclosure_policy.current: SECURITY.md describes private reporting via GitHub Security Advisories.
gaps: No formal VDP with expected response times
vulnerability_disclosure_policy.recommendation: Create formal VDP following ISO 29147 / OpenSSF guidelines. Publish on static site.

analysis.local_first_mode: User is data controller. Rig Relay software runs on user's machine. No data processed by Rig Relay maintainer. Agent-client-protocol defines ACP relay behavior.
analysis.hosted_mode_future: Rig Relay maintainer becomes data processor. User remains data controller. DPA required.
analysis.llm_providers: LLM providers (DeepSeek, OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) are subprocessors when user sends prompts. Rig Relay does not intermediate this relationship.
analysis.github_integration: GitHub is a separate data controller for repository data. Rig Relay accesses via user-authorized OAuth tokens.

data_processing_roles.recommendation: Document data processing roles clearly. For local-first: no processor relationship with maintainer. For hosted: DPA required. Disclose LLM provider subprocessor relationships.

open_source_vs_hosted_enterprise_boundar.current_state: Rig Relay is open-source (AGPL) with local-first architecture. No hosted service exists.
open_source_vs_hosted_enterprise_boundar.future_state: Enterprise hosted service would be separate from open-source project. May require different license, terms, and infrastructure.
boundary_questions: Will open-source and enterprise be the same codebase or a fork?
Will enterprise features be proprietary or open-core?
How will contributions be managed across open-source and enterprise?
Will AGPL apply to enterprise hosted service?
open_source_vs_hosted_enterprise_boundar.recommendation: Define open-source vs enterprise boundary clearly. Consider open-core model: core is AGPL, enterprise features are commercial. Document contribution flow for both.

claims_that_can_be_made_today: Rig Relay is a local-first governed coding agent runtime
Product telemetry is first-party, enabled by default, and opt-out. Remote telemetry contribution is separately settings-controlled and default-off
No raw code, secrets, or private data in any telemetry or evidence layer (content-light guarantee)
Aggregated, de-identified, or derived product intelligence may be commercialized. Raw user content, prompts, credentials, secrets, private files, and private repository contents are never sold
Receipt-backed evidence for all tool execution
claims_that_cannot_be_made_today: GDPR compliant (no DPA, no formal privacy program)
Enterprise-grade security (no pen test, no third-party assessment)
Supply-chain secure (no SBOM, no dependency scanning, no artifact signing)

summary.overall_status: Legal and commercial foundation is minimal. AGPL license, missing DPA, missing terms of service, and missing commercial licensing path are blockers for enterprise procurement.
blockers: AGPL-only licensing — need commercial license option
No DPA or data processing role definition
No terms of service or acceptable use policy
